title: Choose Cortex's visual world (bolder hand)
question: Bolder re-roll, steered to intelligent colour and a futuristic product feel. The deal leads with Datamatics.

options.label: Datamatics
options.lineage: data-sublime installations: hairline bar fields, monospace numerics, one-frame inversions
options.thesis: The agent's research is drawn as a live data field: every search and every piece of evidence is a hairline bar, coloured by its source.
options.viewport: Black shell, thin left rail. A centred question and answer column. Above the answer, a slim evidence field: one hairline bar per evidence item, its length the step's real duration and its hue the source; it settles into the citation index when verification ends. Ask bar at the foot, with a monospace status line.
options.risk: Strobing or too much field turns it into a screensaver; the field must stay one slim band and freeze under reduced motion.

raised.raise: Colour by division: each source owns one full-strength hue, used identically in bars, citations, evidence rows and connection tiles. That is the 'intelligent colour' system.
A bar's length is the step's exact duration, so the trace doubles as a timing chart.
Every claim sits next to its proof: hovering a citation lifts that evidence row inline.
Action states stamp on and never vanish: Approved, Sent, Declined stay visible on the card.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Cortex as a visible construction grid: the wordmark and key numbers are built cell by cell, and the layout grid stays faintly visible.
options.viewport: Dark ultramarine ground with a faint cell grid; groundedness score and step counts set in grid-built numerals; standard nav and answer column.
options.case: Holds audience identification for 'futuristic' (1960s modernist future), but the visible grid competes with reading answers.
options.risk: The grid becomes decoration if it shows behind body text.

options.label: Jet-age ticket wallet
options.thesis: Actions as tear-off coupons stamped validated or void.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro rather than futuristic, and only the actions map cleanly.
options.kept: States stamp on and never disappear.

options.label: Monochrome product
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white, one accent, every claim paired with proof.
options.case: Loses both axes: it's the category look you steered away from, with no intelligent colour.
options.kept: Every claim sits next to its proof.

options.label: Dance score
options.thesis: Time flows upward; block length is exact duration.
options.case: Loses both axes: unfamiliar notation, upward time confuses reading.

options.label: Acetate tab manual
options.lineage: boxed-software manuals with colour divider tabs
options.thesis: Each division owns a full-strength hue; acetate leaves float above.
options.case: Loses both axes: print-era material, layered leaves hurt legibility.
options.kept: Colour by division, applied everywhere (became the source-hue system).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Perplexity/Linear-style neutral assistant, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Grey sidebar, centred chat column, rounded answer card, sources as a chip row.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every AI wrapper by design.
